attacks: Unsigned app persistence: an app package that is not signed is installed and started with the session.

title: Windows Recall can save snapshots of the screen
detail: The Recall feature is enabled and no policy keeps snapshots off.
attacks: Data theft from screen history: an infostealer reads the Recall database, with everything the user saw, passwords and messages included.

title: Linux distribution installed under WSL
detail: jsmith has the Linux distribution Ubuntu-24.04 registered in WSL 2 (a lightweight virtual machine).
attacks: Hiding from the EDR: an attacker runs tools, scanners and scripts inside the Linux distribution, where Windows security tools and logs do not look.

title: Hyper-V or Windows Sandbox turned on on a workstation
detail: The Hyper-V feature (Microsoft-Hyper-V-All) is turned on on this workstation.
attacks: Hiding in a virtual machine: ransomware or an attacker runs a small virtual machine, out of sight of the host's EDR, and works on the user's files and the shares from inside it.

title: Named pipe that everyone can write to
detail: \\.\pipe\FabrikamUpdaterPipe may be written to by Everyone, Authenticated Users (41 of 180 pipes read, the others were busy).
attacks: Privilege escalation: a local user, or anyone through SMB when anonymous logons may write, sends crafted requests to a service running as SYSTEM.

title: Office add-in that is not signed
detail: Excel loads PriceSync.Connect for jsmith from C:\Users\jsmith\AppData\Roaming\PriceSync\pricesync64.dll, signature NotSigned.
attacks: Office persistence: an add-in starts with every Office application, reads the user's documents and mail, and comes back at each start.

title: Windows credentials saved in Credential Manager
detail: jsmith has 14 credential file(s) saved in Credential Manager (more than 10).
attacks: Credential theft: an infostealer or an attacker in the session decrypts the saved passwords and tokens and reuses them on other servers and cloud services.

title: Shadow copies or System Restore turned off
detail: The Volume Shadow Copy service is disabled: no shadow copies, previous versions or VSS backups.
attacks: No local recovery from ransomware: with shadow copies and restore points gone, encrypted or deleted files cannot be brought back from the host itself.

title: Shadow copies or System Restore turned off
detail: The policy "Turn off System Restore" is on: no restore points are made.
attacks: No local recovery from ransomware: with shadow copies and restore points gone, encrypted or deleted files cannot be brought back from the host itself.

title: Windows Hello keys kept without a TPM
detail: Windows Hello is in use without a working TPM: its keys are kept in software.
found: no TPM, 1 user(s) with a PIN
attacks: Credential theft: with SYSTEM rights an attacker copies the Windows Hello keys stored in software and, with the PIN, signs in as the user.

title: Firewall lets in connections to a program in a user folder
detail: 2 inbound allow rule(s) for C:\Users\jsmith\Downloads\AnyDesk.exe, profile Public, from any address.
attacks: Entry through the firewall: whoever replaces the program in the user folder receives connections from the network, a public Wi-Fi included.

title: RDP enabled on a workstation
detail: fDenyTSConnections = 0.
cis_benchmark: CIS Microsoft Windows 11 Enterprise Benchmark v3.0.0
attacks: Remote access and lateral movement: RDP on a workstation is a target for password attacks and lets an attacker with credentials take over the desktop remotely.

title: Built-in Administrator enabled
detail: Enabled; LAPS manages its password.
attacks: Password attacks on a known account: the RID-500 Administrator exists on every host, is exempt from lockout by default, and its shared password lets an attacker move from host to host (pass-the-hash).

title: Administrator protection not turned on
detail: TypeOfAdminApprovalMode = 1: elevation still uses the split token of the signed-in administrator.
attacks: UAC bypass: malware running as an administrator elevates silently through the many known bypasses of the split-token Admin Approval Mode.

title: Local account password probably shared with other hosts
detail: Built-in Administrator (RID 500), password set 2026-09-25 00:00:00 UTC here and on 1 other host(s): WKS-HR-004.
attacks: Pass-the-hash across the fleet: the hash of the shared local password, taken from one host, logs on to all the others.

title: Local account password probably shared with other hosts
detail: Built-in Administrator (RID 500), password set 2026-09-25 00:00:00 UTC here and on 1 other host(s): SRV-APP-02.
attacks: Pass-the-hash across the fleet: the hash of the shared local password, taken from one host, logs on to all the others.
